newsitem.title: EGYPT: Group says Israel seeks Palestinian civil war.
newsitem.headline: Group says Israel seeks Palestinian civil war.

text.p: A leader of the militant Palestinian group Islamic Jihad said in comments published on Monday that Israel wanted to spark Palestinian civil war by insisting that Palestinian leaders clamp down on "terrorism".

Israel has accused the Palestinian Authority of not doing enough to fight anti-Israeli guerrillas in its territory after a double suicide bombing that killed the two bombers and 14 other people in Jerusalem last month.

"With these demands, Israel wants to create violent discord and ignite a Palestinian civil war, but we will never allow our nation to be turned into a new Afghanistan, Somalia or even Algeria and we hope the Authority is aware of such a danger," Ramadan Abdullah Shallah, secretary-general of Islamic Jihad, told the London-based daily al-Hayat.

"Israel knows that the Palestinian people are the infrastructure of Hamas and Jihad and hitting this foundation to uproot them means declaring a war of annihilation against these people who give birth to martyrs and this is impossible.
"As long as these people remain and as long as there are mosques and Islam, then Hamas, Jihad and all the resistance movements will remain," Shallah said.
Islamic Jihad and Hamas are members of a 10-member radical Palestinian alliance that vowed to wreck a peace deal between Israel and the Palestinians.

Hamas's armed wing claimed responsibility for last month's suicide attacks in a leaflet whose credibility has been questioned by Israeli and Palestinian officials. The attackers have yet to be identified.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat has rejected Israeli allegations that his planned "national unity" talks with militant Palestinian groups set for this week were an "appeasement of terrorism."
"If the PLO liberated itself from the Oslo (peace) agreement and resumed armed struggle we would accept to join it within a unifying framework for our people's struggle," Shallah said.
He said the United States was too biased to be of any help as a mediator.

"What do you expect when the Jewish (U.S. Secretary of State) Madeleine Albright sends the Jewish Ross to talk to the Jewish Netanyahu? What good can Palestinians or Arabs gain from this trinity that represents an administration that is more Zionist than the Israeli Knesset (parliament)?" he said.
